## Task
Today four people need one combined table for hosting, using both tables and all four stools. Arrange the four places while preserving the rest of the home.

This is an 8x7m researcher reconstruction, not the measured Waterloo apartment. Keep all 27 object instances and existing asset sizes. Only the two tables and four stools are movable; retain bed, living, kitchen, bathroom, storage and window access. All four stools must remain even when only two are in use. Do not add, remove, replace, scale or change fixtures. Tables are generated rectangular wheeled meshes, 1.2x0.7m and 0.74m high; stools are 0.44m square and 0.45m high. These wheels are not articulated. All coordinates are local metres. For this task the separated-table condition means at least 0.6m between table footprints, with recon_chair_a_0 and recon_chair_b_0 each serving a different table. The hosting condition means parallel, same-height tables joined end-to-end with at most 0.05m gap and at most 0.03m offset across their widths; one stool at each long edge of each table provides four nonoverlapping 0.4x0.25m tabletop places, with stool-to-table edge gaps 0.05 to 0.4m. Either table may move, and stool/table assignment is not fixed. No target coordinates are provided. Use the supplied actual geometry/access feedback to preserve all seven approach points at 0.4/0.5/0.6m square-body widths; grid 0.02m, height1.8m, doors assumed open. These dimensions and mode tests are researcher task criteria, not ergonomic standards. Seated comfort, load, brakes, human handling and full facility operation remain unknown. The original resident brief is unavailable; the following request is researcher constructed. Stop when the current request is satisfied; unnecessary edits also consume budget.
